title: Vietnamese Rice Paper Rolls
subtitle: with peanut dipping sauce
menu_blurb: Gỏi cuốn: marinated tofu, butter lettuce, cucumber, carrot, avocado and fresh mint, wrapped in delicate rice paper. Fresh, light, and never fried.
intro: Packed with bright, fresh ingredients and served with an insanely delicious peanut dipping sauce. Also known as gỏi cuốn, or summer rolls, they make a fresh, light, and healthy Vietnamese appetizer or snack.
origin: Rice paper rolls (gỏi cuốn) come from South Vietnam, a staple dish born from local agricultural traditions. They are characterized by fresh herbs, a protein (tofu, pork, or shrimp), and vermicelli wrapped in thin, edible rice paper (bánh tráng). Known as “salad rolls” in the South and “nem cuốn” in the North, they are a healthy, fresh, non-fried alternative to traditional spring rolls.

mise_en_place.label: Marinate
mise_en_place.task: Tofu in soy sauce, ponzu, garlic, and red pepper flakes

mise_en_place.label: Soak
mise_en_place.task: Rice noodles in boiling water until softened

mise_en_place.label: Chop
mise_en_place.task: Lettuce, tofu, carrots, cucumbers, and avocado

steps.title: Prepare
instructions: **Tofu:** slice and marinate in the soy sauce, ponzu, and chopped garlic.
**Vegetables:** cut each one and arrange each type on its own plate.
**Rice noodles:** place in a bowl of boiling water to soften, about 5 to 8 minutes.

steps.title: Pre-cook
instructions: Place the tofu on the griddle (or air fry it) and lightly sauté on both sides. Set on a plate to cool.

steps.title: Form the rolls
instructions: Have all of your ingredients in front of you.
Hold a sheet of rice paper and quickly dip it under water.
Lay it on a plate and gently massage it until pliable.
Add the fillings one at a time.
note: **Authentic gỏi cuốn:** lettuce, tofu, bean sprouts, rice noodles, carrots, and mint, with sesame seeds on top, folded into a square. *Tip:* wrap the tofu, bean sprouts, vermicelli, and mint in the lettuce first, then roll or lightly scrunch it so it holds together before rolling it in the rice paper. Much easier to handle!
**My summer rolls:** tofu, avocado, carrots, and cucumbers, folded like an egg roll.

steps.title: Fold and roll tightly
instructions: Fold the sides in first, then roll to the end, like an egg roll. You can also fold them into a square.

steps.title: Griddle to crisp
instructions: Place some of the rolls on the griddle with a sprinkle of sesame seeds and turn until crispy on both sides.

sauce.title: Peanut Sauce
sauce.method: Combine the sauce ingredients and mix briefly (it won’t come together right away), then microwave for 30 seconds. Mix again until smooth and set aside to cool. Adjust the sourness with vinegar, the saltiness with salt, and the spice to taste. Once cooled, thin with milk or water as needed.

items.name: Peanut butter, preferably smooth (crunchy is fine too)
Sweet soy sauce (kecap manis, thick like syrup)

tips.label: Substitution
tips.tip: Vary the fillings. Firm tofu works too, but press out all the water before cooking. You can also add other cooked proteins, such as shrimp, chicken, or pork.

tips.label: Meal prep hack
tips.tip: Don’t make these ahead. Prepare them and serve immediately, since the rolls don’t last long in the refrigerator. A damp paper towel on top helps keep them fresh.

Made from rice flour, rice noodles are a quickly digested, high-energy carb. Gluten-free, a good source of selenium, with modest manganese and phosphorus.

notebook.question: What is tofu, and is it good for you?
answer: Tofu is a nutrient-dense, plant-based protein made from curdled soy milk pressed into blocks. It is a complete protein, containing all nine essential amino acids, and it is high in iron and calcium. It is generally considered very healthy: it supports heart health, may reduce the risk of certain cancers, and aids weight management. It is low in fat, cholesterol-free, and safe to eat every day.
Its nutrition varies mainly with firmness. Firmer varieties hold less water, so they carry more protein, fat, and calories per serving.

table.label: Extra firm
table.text: 15 to 17 g protein and about 145 calories

table.label: Firm
table.text: 8 to 10 g protein and 70 to 80 calories

table.label: Silken or soft
table.text: Higher in water, with about 4 to 7 g protein and 40 to 62 calories

benefits.label: Heart health
benefits.text: Cholesterol-free and low in saturated fat, tofu may help reduce LDL cholesterol. Studies show eating at least one serving a week may lower heart disease risk by 18%.

benefits.label: Nutrient-rich
benefits.text: A good source of iron, manganese, selenium, phosphorus, and calcium, especially when made with calcium sulfate.

benefits.label: Cancer risk reduction
benefits.text: Tofu contains isoflavones, which have antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties and potential protective effects against breast, prostate, and colorectal cancers.

benefits.label: Bone health
benefits.text: Its high calcium and magnesium content helps prevent osteoporosis.
